facts.raw_span: a 4-year history of a slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion
a 1 cm × 0.5 cm macule, which progressively increased in size without symptoms
brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion
multiple pigmented papules of various sizes involved the vermilion of the upper left lip
brownish skin discoloration extending from 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth to the left philtral ridge
the lip was slightly swollen
a 1.5 cm lesion extended from the labial frenum to 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth
it was non-tender, non-indurated, and exhibited focal ulcerations
no cervical lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions were found
Results of a complete blood count, biochemical profile, and urinalysis were within normal limits
chest radiography was unremarkable
a computed tomography scan of the head and neck was performed to assess local extent of the lesion and to evaluate regional lymph nodes
